Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Holdings's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Credit Officer; David Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Marketing Officer; and Karen Lopez, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Holdings delivered record results in the Q3 2024, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Sustaining strong revenue growth
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Investing in technology and innovation
5. Enhancing customer experience
6. Strengthening our brand reputation
7. Promoting a diverse and inclusive culture
8. Delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on:
Our outlook for loan growth and credit quality remains resilient, with mid-single-digit expansion expected while upholding superior metrics; 
Cost of deposits is rising amid competition, but our strategies are stabilizing betas; 
Fee income across wealth management, investment banking, and cards showed robust growth from market tailwinds and digital initiatives; 
Capital return plans emphasize progressive dividends and opportunistic repurchases; 
Asset sensitivity positions us well for rate changes with proactive hedging; 
NII trends reflect solid YoY and QoQ gains from yield improvements; 
Efficiency ratio progress is accelerating toward mid-50s targets; 
Provision for credit losses balances caution with economic resilience.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Holdings reported net income of $1.5 billion for the Q3 2024, or $2.95 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8% year-over-year, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 14% year-over-year, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. Turning now to our outlook for loan growth and credit quality, I'm pleased to report a resilient picture underpinned by disciplined underwriting, diversified portfolio management, and proactive risk mitigation strategies. As we navigate a higher-for-longer interest rate environment—echoing the Fed's recent 25-basis-point hike to 5.25-5.50%—our balance sheet remains well-positioned to deliver mid-single-digit growth while maintaining pristine credit metrics.

Starting with loan growth, we delivered a robust 5.2% year-over-year increase in Q3, bringing average loans to $285 billion, driven primarily by our commercial and industrial (C&I) and specialty lending segments. Commercial Banking saw C&I loans grow 7.1% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by capital expenditure cycles in manufacturing and tech sectors. We're seeing strong pipeline momentum from middle-market clients—think regional players akin to our partnerships with firms like Caterpillar and regional SaaS providers—where utilization rates have ticked up to 52% from 48% a year ago. CRE exposure remains selective; office loans are flat at $42 billion, with no new commitments in Class B/C properties amid remote work trends, but multifamily and industrial portfolios expanded 4% on robust demand in Sun Belt markets like Texas and Florida.

Consumer and Mortgage: Consumer loans, including auto and credit card, rose 3.8% to $68 billion, supported by our digital origination platform—which processed 1.2 million applications via our mobile app in Q3, up 25% YoY. Mortgage originations were softer at $15 billion quarterly, reflecting 7% rates, but our jumbo and HELOC products grew 6%, capturing high-net-worth clients migrating from competitors like Rocket Mortgage.

Global and Wholesale: International loans, 22% of total, advanced 4.5%, with strength in Asia-Pacific trade finance (up 8%) leveraging our blockchain-based platform in partnership with HSBC-inspired consortia for supply chain efficiency.

Looking forward, we guide to full-year 2024 loan growth of 4.5-6%, with an average of $290 billion by year-end, modestly ahead of our prior 4-5.5% outlook. This assumes GDP growth of 2.1% as per the latest Atlanta Fed GDPNow tracker, stable unemployment at 4.1%, and no recessionary pull-forward. For 2025, we're targeting 5-7% growth, accelerating on expected Fed cuts—potentially 75-100 bps by mid-year—unlocking pent-up corporate demand and refinancing activity. Key enablers include our AI-driven dynamic pricing engine, which has improved approval rates by 15% while optimizing yields, and expansion of our "Green Loans" product suite, now at $12 billion committed for ESG-linked projects, mirroring trends at peers like Bank of America.

We've also launched a $500 million targeted growth initiative in equipment finance, partnering with John Deere Financial analogs, projecting 10-12% segment growth amid infrastructure spending from the IIJA.

On credit quality, our metrics continue to outperform industry benchmarks. Q3 net charge-offs were a pristine 28 basis points, down from 32 bps in Q2 and well below the 10-year average of 45 bps per S&P data. Delinquencies over 30 days stood at 0.78%, versus 0.92% last quarter and the industry's 1.05% median. Our CECL reserve stands at 1.12% of loans, or $3.2 billion, with a coverage ratio of 285% on criticized loans—reflecting conservative provisioning ahead of any softening.

Critically, no systemic stresses: Consumer delinquencies are stable at 1.1% (autos at 0.9%, cards at 1.8%), buoyed by wage growth outpacing inflation. Commercial saw NPLs tick to 0.65% from 0.58%, isolated to a handful of healthcare and energy credits, but our 90+ day delinquencies remain under 0.2%. CRE office is our watchful area—migration to 0.4% NPLs—but LTVs average 62%, with 85% floating-rate structures repricing higher.

Regionally, Southeast US performance is exemplary, with charge-offs at 22 bps versus national 35 bps, thanks to diversified exposure to logistics and data centers. Conversely, we're de-risking Northeast CRE, reducing office commitments by 15% YoY.

Strategically, we're enhancing resilience through advanced analytics: Rolled out GenAI-enhanced credit scoring models in Q1, incorporating alternative data like cash flow volatility and climate risk proxies, reducing expected losses by 8-10% in backtests—similar to JPMorgan's COiN platform evolution.

Stress testing and hedging: Quarterly CCAR-like internal stresses assume 50 bps higher unemployment and 200 bps rate shocks; our CET1 buffer of 12.8% absorbs this with room to spare. We've layered $2.5 billion in credit default swaps on vulnerable sectors.

Portfolio diversification: Non-U.S. loans now 25% (up from 20%), with emphasis on high-growth EMs via our IFC-inspired sustainable finance desk.

In summary, loan growth remains our top priority for organic balance sheet expansion, paired with fortress-like credit quality. We're not chasing volume at the expense of risk, positioning us to outperform in any scenario—be it soft landing or mild downturn.

Good morning, everyone. Before I hand it over for other updates, let me dive deeper into our deposit franchise, specifically our cost of deposits, average rates, and the competitive dynamics shaping this critical funding source. Deposits remain the bedrock of our low-cost, stable funding model, comprising 92% of our total funding mix at quarter-end, with a loan-to-deposit ratio of 78%—well below the peer median of 85%. However, in this high-rate environment, we've seen meaningful upward pressure on deposit pricing, which has tempered our net interest margin expansion.

Our average cost of deposits in Q3 rose 28 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 2.47%, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration. Year-over-year, that's a 132 basis point increase from the ultra-low 1.15% in Q3 2023. This reflects a deposit beta of approximately 52% to date on the Fed's 525 basis point hiking cycle since March 2022—right in line with regional peers like Regions Financial and Synovus, but slightly ahead of super-regionals like PNC at 48%. Total deposit interest expense climbed 22% quarter-over-quarter to $285 million, driven by both rate and modest 2.1% volume growth to $142 billion in average balances.

Breaking it down by deposit beta cohorts, our core transaction and savings deposits—85% of the mix—averaged 1.92% in cost, up 18 bps QoQ. These sticky, low-beta accounts benefited from our relationship-driven model, where 62% are tied to commercial or consumer loan relationships, insulating us somewhat from beta bleed. Non-interest-bearing demand deposit accounts (DDAs) held steady at 22% of total deposits, costing us effectively zero, though we've seen some migration to interest-bearing options amid competitive offers. On the higher end, time deposits and brokered CDs, now 12% of the mix (up from 8% a year ago), carried a 4.65% average rate—up 45 bps QoQ—as we selectively added wholesale funding to support loan growth in our C&I and CRE portfolios.

Competitive pressures are intensifying across the board, exacerbated by the inverted yield curve and alternatives like money market funds yielding 5.2% on average per iMoneyNet data, Treasury bills at SOFR-plus spreads, and fintech disruptors. Nationally, online banks like Ally and Marcus by Goldman Sachs are advertising 4.2-4.5% APYs on high-yield savings accounts (HYSAs), pulling retail deposits away from traditional players. Among banks, promotional CD rates have surged: JPMorgan's 4.75% 5-month special versus our 4.10% ladder average, and regional competitors like Fifth Third offering 4.3% on relationship CDs in key markets. Our deposit pricing analytics show us paying a 15-20 bps premium in urban footprints like Miami and Nashville to retain high-net-worth clients against private banks such as First Republic remnants now under JPM.

Regionally, in our Southeast core markets (Georgia, Florida, Tennessee), where we hold 4.2% deposit market share per S&P Global data, average costs moderated to 2.28%, supported by strong commercial deposit inflows from healthcare and manufacturing relationships. These 'sticky' deposits exhibit betas under 40%, thanks to treasury management services like our UniCash platform, which locks in balances via zero-balance sweeps. Conversely, in expansion markets like Texas and California—where we're scaling via de novo branches and tuck-in acquisitions—costs hit 2.85%, pressured by tech-driven wealth migration to fintechs like SoFi (offering 4.5% checking with direct deposit) and brokered CD competition from money-center banks. California deposit betas are tracking 60%, reflecting affluent customers chasing yield.

Strategically, dynamic relationship pricing engine rolled out in Q1 via our core banking upgrade with FIS, this AI-driven tool segments customers by lifetime value and offers personalized rates—e.g., capping HYSA at 3.75% for non-relationship holders but tiering up to 4.25% for $500k+ loans. Early results: reduced beta expansion by 10 bps in test markets.

Digital retention suite: Our revamped mobile app now features 'Deposit Optimizer,' a gamified tool recommending ladders and auto-sweeps into CDs, boosting digital deposit retention 15% QoQ. We're also piloting blockchain-based tokenized deposits with partners like Provenance for institutional clients, targeting sub-2% costs on $2B+ balances.

Wholesale alternatives and hedging: To avoid overpaying on retail CDs, we've capped brokered CDs at 10% of funding via FHLB advances at 4.8% (blended with swaps) and explored match-term repos. This kept our marginal funding cost at 4.1%, 35 bps below peers.

Branch and marketing discipline: Rationalized 12 underperforming branches in high-cost markets, reallocating to digital acquisition, and ramped targeted campaigns emphasizing FDIC insurance and service over pure rate—'Rate Plus Service' positioning, which stabilized retail inflows.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 deposit costs to rise another 15-20 bps to 2.62-2.67%, assuming Fed funds hold at 5.25-5.50%. Full-year beta should moderate to 48-50% as repricing matures, with core deposits stabilizing above 85% mix. Our franchise strength—evidenced by 92% retention rate—positions us for NIM expansion to 3.55% by year-end.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving into other areas, let me highlight our non-interest income performance, which continues to be a key growth engine for UniBank Holdings. Total fee income reached $2.8 billion in the quarter, up 14% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, representing 28% of our total revenue mix—our strongest quarterly showing since Q4 2021. This outperformance was driven by resilient client activity across our franchises, favorable market tailwinds, and the early benefits from our 'UniWealth Digital 2.0' platform rollout. Excluding a one-time $150 million gain from a structured products unwind, core fee income grew 11%.

Wealth management fees hit $1.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year and now comprising 50% of total fee income—our largest and most stable contributor. Assets under management, or AUM, expanded to $1.2 trillion, a 12% increase from year-end 2023, with net new money inflows of $28 billion in the quarter alone, exceeding our full-year guidance midpoint of $90-100 billion.

Key drivers: Market appreciation as equities rallied 8% in Q3, led by the S&P 500's tech-heavy gains, boosting advisory and performance fees by 22%. Our model portfolios, benchmarked against the MSCI World Index, outperformed by 150 basis points net of fees. Product mix shift: Recurring revenue from ETFs and alternatives grew 25%, with $12 billion in inflows to our UniAlternatives platform—private credit and infrastructure funds, yielding 45-65 bps on AUM versus 25-35 bps on traditional equities.

Regional strength: APAC was the standout, with 35% YoY fee growth to $420 million, driven by HNW client acquisition in Singapore and Hong Kong amid China's property stabilization. EMEA added 15% growth via our London wealth hub, capitalizing on UK pension consolidation flows.

Technical initiatives: Our UniWealth Digital 2.0 app, launched in June, now has 1.2 million active users—up 40% QoQ—with AI-driven personalization boosting cross-sell ratios by 18%. Robo-advisory AUM hit $150 billion, with churn under 2%. We're doubling down on sustainable investing; ESG-linked products now represent 28% of AUM, with $8 billion in new mandates. Margins held at 42%.

Investment banking fees came in at $720 million, a robust 22% YoY increase and 9% QoQ, accounting for 26% of fee income. League tables underscore our momentum: #4 in global M&A advisory and #3 in EMEA ECM.

Deal flow recovery: Global M&A volume rose 15% QoQ to $1.1 trillion, with our advisory fees up 28% to $380 million on 45 completed deals—average fee of 1.2%. Highlights included advising on the $25 billion AstraZeneca spin-off and a $12 billion private equity take-private in industrials. Capital markets tailwinds: ECM fees jumped 35% to $210 million, fueled by 12 IPOs and follow-ons raising $18 billion total. Debt underwriting added $130 million.

Regional: Americas dominated at 55% of fees, leveraging our NYIB franchise. APAC grew 18% on Greater China listings. Tech enablers: Our IBXpert AI tool accelerated pitch win rates to 32%, cloud migration reduced execution time by 20%. Pipeline up 30% QoQ positions us for H2 acceleration. Fee margins expanded to 38%.

Cards and payments fees totaled $680 million, up 8% YoY and flat QoQ, 24% of fee income. Processed $450 billion in volume, +11% YoY, with 45 million active accounts. Spending resilience: Consumer spend grew 9% in travel and entertainment. Interchange revenue rose 10% to $420 million, blended yield 1.85%. Premium segment: UniBlack and UniReserve cards drove 22% fee growth. Partnerships boosted acquisition by 12%. Regional: US +10%, Europe +6%, EM +15%. Tokenization hit 92% of transactions, reducing fraud 30%. Embedded finance added $50 million.

In summary, fee income's 14% growth reflects balanced strength, with Q4 guide $2.9-3.1 billion.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. Turning now to our capital return plans, including dividends and share repurchases, our disciplined approach has delivered consistent shareholder value while maintaining a fortress balance sheet. CET1 ratio at 11.8%, up 20 bps QoQ, above 10.5% target. SLR 6.2%, CCAR stress decline 240 bps.

Dividends: Quarterly $0.58 per share, up 9% YoY, annualized yield 3.2%. TTM payout 42%. Paid $1.8 billion YTD.

Share repurchases: $3.2 billion YTD under $6 billion authorization, 200 bps EPS accretion. Paused when below 1.1x TBV, resumed post-stabilization.

Regionally tailored: US robust growth, Europe ECB tailwinds, APAC undervaluation.

2025 outlook: $8-9 billion organic capital. Dividend to $0.65 quarterly, 45% payout on $8.50 EPS. New $8 billion repurchase program, total yield 8-10%.

Risks mitigated via securities optimization. Strategy prioritizes sustainability above 12% ROCE.

Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Before we open the line for Q&A, I'd like to provide some color on our asset sensitivity position and broader interest rate risk management framework. NII sensitivity at 28% for +100 bps shift. -100 bps shock: $45 million headwind, offset by NIB deposits 22%.

Repricing gap positive $18.2 billion 0-12 months, from floating C&I 65% at SOFR. EVE -3.8% +200 bps shock. $7.5 billion receive-fixed swaps at 4.85%.

Trends: Deposit betas 65%, loan 92%. Regional: US sticky Southeast, Europe hedged, APAC collars.

Initiatives: $15 million IRRBB modeling upgrade to Monte Carlo, VaR +22%. $5 billion securities reposition: sold $1.2 billion corporates, into SOFR MBS, duration gap to 1.4 years.

Forward: Loan pipeline $8.7 billion. Stress-tested scenarios show optionality, CET1 11.8%. NII margins 3.65%, guide raised.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our core profitability driver: net interest income, or NII, which came in at $2.52 billion for the quarter, a solid 6% increase QoQ from $2.38 billion in Q2, and 8.2% rise YoY from $2.33 billion in Q3 2023. NIM to 3.48%, +10 bps QoQ, asset yields +22 bps to 5.62% from C&I reset, securities optimization.

Funding: Deposit costs +15 bps to 2.14%, betas 45%. YoY: NIM +28 bps, asset yields +85 bps, deposit costs +110 bps.

Regional: US +10%, Europe +4%, APAC +15%. Initiatives: ALM hedging 40%, digital deposits, embedded finance.

Q4 NII $2.55-2.60 billion, NIM 3.45-3.50%.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. Moving now to our efficiency ratio, at 54.2%, 280 bps QoQ improvement from 57.0%, 720 bps YoY from 61.4%, ahead of peer median 58.1%. Expenses down 7% to $2.85 billion vs revenue +4% to $5.26 billion.

Levers: $150 million branch savings, 120 closures. Tech: $80 million from Temenos cloud, RPA 40% automation, AI chatbot 65% inquiries.

Regional: North America 52.8%, Europe 58.5%, APAC 49.7%. Supports ROTE 12.8%, Q4 target 53.0%, FY2024 54.5%, 50% FY2025.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to dive into our provision for credit losses, or PCL, at $450 million for Q3, +15% QoQ from $390 million, but -10% YoY from $500 million. Allowance $12.8 billion, 2.5x NCO coverage.

Drivers: CRE $120 million from office stress, consumer $180 million auto caution, C&I $110 million manufacturing, international offset.

Regional: US 65%, Europe 20%, EM 15%. CECL methodology: PD/LGD/EAD, 36-month forecast, scenarios weighted 60/30/10.

Enhancements: GenAI early warning -18% error, qualitative +$30 million. NCO $320 million 85 bps. Derisking: CRE -5% QoQ, tighter underwriting. Q1 2025 $400-500 million.

That covers our financial details.

Michael Torres:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, commercial real estate exposure, deposit competition, and geopolitical tensions. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Lisa Chen:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with net charge-offs at 28 basis points and delinquencies at 0.78%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

David Patel:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI-driven credit scoring and cloud-native platforms are yielding significant results.

Emily Vargas:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making.

Robert Kline:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention.

Karen Lopez:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Susan Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Susan Lee:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on outlook for loan growth and credit quality?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Susan. As Sarah outlined extensively, we're guiding 4.5-6% full-year growth with pristine metrics like 28 bps charge-offs and robust reserves. Our diversified approach and AI tools keep us ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Bradley with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Bradley:
What is your outlook for NII trends?

Sarah Jenkins:
Thanks, Tom. We see Q4 at $2.55-2.60 billion with stable NIM, supported by asset yields and hedging, even with potential cuts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Can you discuss the impact of asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management?

Michael Torres:
Absolutely, Mike. Our positive gap and $7.5 billion in swaps provide resilience, with minimal NII impact from cuts and strong stress results.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim:
What are your plans for technology in deposit and credit initiatives?

David Patel:
Great question, Laura. We're expanding AI pricing, GenAI scoring, and digital tools like Deposit Optimizer, delivering efficiency and growth as detailed.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
